findings.rationale: The accepted claims cover soul–body separation and purification, practice of dying, philosophical versus body-directed motives, and the contrast between philosophical and conventional courage and temperance. The commentary remains interpretive, source-compatible, and coherent.

All title and body assertions have exact accepted support: obs_phaedo_0073 covers Simmias’ request; claims 0087 and 0091 cover sensible equals’ apparent inequality and deficiency; claim 0089 covers conception from perception; claim 0097 covers prior knowledge. The section is coherent and remains enc

Claims 0170 and 0176 exactly support the harmony’s following of bodily elements and the soul’s opposition to bodily affections. The framing coherently synthesizes these points within 92d–96c; “voice” is interpretive rather than an additional factual claim.

Claims 0237–0241 directly support Cebes’s acceptance, Socrates’ methodological re-examination, the conditional need for care, and the explicitly reported traditional postmortem account. The hinge framing synthesizes these without asserting an unproved doctrine or importing 114d cosmology.

The myth framing and limited-perspective claims are supported by obs_phaedo_0228–0230; the qualification against treating the account as exactly true is supported by obs_phaedo_0246. The interpretive framing remains compatible with the Greek anchor.
